prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the steep vertical drop from the rocky ledge where the camera wearer stands down to the dirt trail below on the right, showing the wearer's hands and smartphone at the bottom-left and bottom-center in frames 1–3 as bright white (~0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach) and the prominent bush in the center-left at mid-range (~1.5–2.5 m away). Below and to the right on the trail (~2.5–3.5 m from the wearer), a hiker with a blue backpack enters at the bottom-right in frame 1 and moves forward-right across frames 2–4, followed closely (~0.5 m behind and to the right) in frames 3–4 by a second hiker in a white jacket before both exit the right/bottom view in frame 5 as the camera shifts left toward the bush. The depth map makes the multi-tiered 3D elevation difference between the foreground ledge, the protruding bush canopy, the two mid-ground hikers on the lower path, and the dark background trail in the upper right (~6–10 m away) much clearer than the top-down RGB strip alone. However, the map is unreliable along fine foliage branches where depth bleeds smoothly into the ground, and in frame 5 where the upper-left foliage brightens inconsistently despite the camera only tilting slightly.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates parts of the foreground and mid-ground people against a black background while omitting the terrain, rocks, and central bush entirely. In frames 1–2, it segments the camera wearer's raised hands and phone on the bottom-left (~0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach) alongside a brown-masked hiker with a blue backpack at the bottom-right (~3 m below on the path) and a tiny cyan mask for a distant person (~8–10 m away) at the top-right of frame 1. Across frames 2–4, as the blue-backpack hiker moves up-right along the lower trail and a white-jacketed hiker appears ~0.5 m to their right/rear, both are segmented at the right edge (partially cropped by the frame boundary and mutually occluding where the first hiker reaches back to hold the second hiker's arm in frame 4), before all masks disappear in frame 5 when the nearby hikers leave the field of view. While the segmentation clearly separates overlapping person regions in frames 3–4, it is highly unreliable: it mislabels the foreground smartphone as a separate 'person' mask in frame 2, splits the white-jacketed hiker into multiple fragmented 'person' masks (cyan and brown) in frame 4, and misses the foreground hands in frame 3 as well as distant hikers in frames 2–5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints on black, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's outstretched right hand (~0.4 m away, within arm's reach at the bottom-left) in frame 2 and nothing at all in frames 1 and 5. In frame 3, it captures the upper-body yellow skeleton and magenta hands of the hiker with the blue backpack (~2.5–3 m below and to the right of the wearer), showing their torso and head angled toward the right along the slope (facing away and not looking at the camera wearer) with both hands near waist/chest level, plus an isolated magenta hand belonging to the adjacent white-jacketed hiker (~0.5 m to their right, holding a small object within their own arm's reach). In frame 4, only the two hikers' proximate magenta hands are detected at the lower right as the blue-backpack hiker's right hand reaches back to grasp the white-jacketed hiker's left arm. Although the pose map clarifies the exact finger articulation of the wearer's hand in frame 2 and the orientation of the hiker's limbs and hands in frames 3–4 better than the cluttered RGB view, it is largely unreliable due to severe top-down foreshortening and partial occlusion, missing whole bodies in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5 and failing to connect the white-jacketed hiker's body skeleton entirely.
